study type: secondary analysis of a multicenter cohort study
cohort: Nulliparous women aged 18 years or older with singleton gestation undergoing labor induction for preeclampsia with severe features and receiving magnesium sulfate.
finding: Lower maternal age and BMI, higher gestational age and Bishop's score on admission, lower admission systolic blood pressure, and interventions like artificial rupture of membranes and oxytocin administration were associated with a higher rate of successful vaginal delivery in this high-risk cohort.
mod_finding: Successful vaginal delivery was associated with improved maternal outcomes (lower postpartum hemorrhage, blood transfusion, composite maternal morbidity) and improved neonatal outcomes (higher 1-minute APGAR, lower NICU admission, lower composite neonatal morbidity).
